overview: Indohyus is pieced together from separately catalogued skulls, teeth and limb bones, not a single complete skeleton. Dense limb bones and isotope measurements from several teeth support an aquatic or wading way of life, while a published phylogenetic analysis places Raoellidae as the sister group of Cetacea. The fossils do not settle diet or complete gait, and the tree does not make Indohyus a crown whale or a demonstrated ancestor.
overviewZh: Indohyus 由分别编目的头骨、牙齿和肢骨拼合认识，并非一副完整骨架。致密肢骨和多颗牙齿的同位素测量支持水生或涉水生活；一项已发表系统发育分析把 Raoellidae 放在鲸类的姐妹群位置。化石没有解决食性或完整步态，树上的关系也不意味着 Indohyus 是冠群鲸类或已证实的直系祖先。

ecology.diet: Diet remains unresolved; the tooth isotopes speak more directly to water use than to food choice.
ecology.habitat: Bone density and tooth isotopes support aquatic or riparian use, but do not record a complete habitat.
ecology.locomotion: Wading is an interpretation; the separately catalogued bones do not preserve a complete gait.
ecology.bodySize: The material represents a small raoellid, on the scale of other small artiodactyls.
ecology.guild: An aquatic or wading ecology is inferred; diet is not resolved.
ecology.dietZh: 食性仍未确定；牙齿同位素更直接反映其用水情况，而非食物选择。
ecology.habitatZh: 骨骼密度和牙齿同位素支持其利用水生或河岸环境，但没有记录完整的生境信息。
ecology.locomotionZh: 涉水是一种解释；另行编目的骨骼没有保存完整步态。
ecology.bodySizeZh: 这些材料代表一种小型饶氏兽科动物，体型与其他小型偶蹄动物相当。
ecology.guildZh: 研究推断其可能具有水生或涉水生态；其食性尚未确定。

traits: Skull material preserves an involucrum, an ear-region thickening compared with cetaceans.
Sections through the long bones show dense bone tissue.
Stable-isotope measurements come from several teeth.
evidenceSummary: These are complementary but separate lines of evidence: a disarticulated bone-bed sample, dense limb bones, tooth isotopes and a phylogenetic analysis. They support aquatic or wading use and a raoellid sister relationship to whales, but leave diet, complete gait and direct ancestry unresolved.
evidenceSummaryZh: 这里的证据彼此互补却回答不同问题：散离骨床材料、致密肢骨、牙齿同位素和系统发育分析共同支持水生或涉水解释，以及 Raoellidae 与鲸类互为姐妹群的关系；食性、完整步态和直系祖先关系仍未解决。

readerLimitations.en: The evidence joins separately catalogued skulls, limb bones and teeth, not an associated skeleton. Bone density and tooth isotopes support aquatic or wading use, but do not settle diet or a complete gait.
readerLimitations.zh: 现有证据把分别编目的头骨、肢骨和牙齿联系起来，并非一具相连骨架。骨密度与牙齿同位素支持水生或涉水解释，却不能确定食性或完整步态。

traitsZh: 颅骨材料保存了鼓泡骨，即鲸类相较之下具有的一种耳区骨性增厚。
长骨切片显示骨组织密度较高。
稳定同位素测量来自多颗牙齿。

overview: The partial Ambulocetus natans skeleton H-GSP 18507 combines strong, weight-bearing limbs with vertebral and hind-limb anatomy used to model movement on land and in water.
overviewZh: Ambulocetus natans 的部分骨架 H-GSP 18507 同时保存了强健、能够负重的肢体，以及用于运动比较的椎骨和后肢解剖。研究者据此讨论陆地行走与水中运动的可能方式；这是根据骨骼建立的功能模型，不是直接观察到的行为。

ecology.diet: Teeth and skull support an inference of aquatic predation, but no prey item is directly documented.
ecology.habitat: An amphibious way of life is inferred from the anatomy and formation context.
ecology.locomotion: Dorsoventral swimming and movement on land are functional models based on preserved anatomy.
ecology.bodySize: The partial skeleton represents a large-bodied early cetacean; it does not establish a full size range.
ecology.guild: The predator interpretation is anatomical inference, not an observed feeding event.
ecology.dietZh: 牙齿和头骨支持其在水中捕食的推断，但没有直接记录到猎物。
ecology.habitatZh: 根据解剖特征和地层背景推断其具有两栖生活方式。
ecology.locomotionZh: 根据保存的解剖特征建立了背腹向游泳和陆上移动的功能模型。
ecology.bodySizeZh: 这具部分骨架代表一种体型较大的早期鲸类；它不能确定完整的体型范围。
ecology.guildZh: 捕食者的解释来自解剖特征推断，并非观察到的摄食事件。

traits: A partial skull and vertebral column
Substantial forelimbs and hind limbs that could bear weight
A mix of vertebral and limb features used in locomotor comparisons
evidenceSummary: The holotype preserves an anatomical mosaic used to infer amphibious movement. Otter-like swimming and sea-lion-like movement on land are comparisons with living animals, not observed behavior or proof of ancestry.
evidenceSummaryZh: 正模保存的骨骼镶嵌被用于推断两栖运动。类似水獭的游泳和类似海狮的陆上移动，是与现生动物作的比较，不是实际行为观察，也不能证明祖先关系。

title.en: How do partial bones support an amphibious model?
title.zh: 残缺骨骼如何支持两栖活动模型？

text.en: The partial Ambulocetus natans skeleton H-GSP 18507 combines strong, weight-bearing limbs with vertebral and hind-limb anatomy used to model movement on land and in water.
text.zh: Ambulocetus natans 的部分骨架 H-GSP 18507 同时保存了强健、能够负重的肢体，以及用于运动比较的椎骨和后肢解剖。研究者据此讨论陆地行走与水中运动的可能方式；这是根据骨骼建立的功能模型，不是直接观察到的行为。

title.en: H-GSP 18507 preserves spine and limb material
title.zh: H-GSP 18507 保存了脊柱和肢骨材料

text.en: The holotype preserves a partial skull and vertebral column together with substantial fore- and hind-limb material. It represents a large-bodied early cetacean. The limbs could bear weight, while the combined vertebral and hind-limb anatomy is what researchers used to compare land and water movement.
text.zh: 正模标本保存了部分头骨和脊柱，并包含相当数量的前肢与后肢材料。它代表一种体型较大的早期鲸类。肢体能够支撑体重；研究者依据脊柱与后肢的组合解剖特征比较其在陆地和水中的运动。

title.zh: 运动方式是重建结果，并非直接观察

text.en: The study infers amphibious movement from anatomy and formation context. Teeth and skull support an aquatic-predation interpretation, but no prey item is directly documented. Dorsoventral swimming, otter-like motion in water and sea-lion-like movement on land are comparisons with living animals, not observed performance.
text.zh: 研究依据解剖结构和地层背景推断其具有两栖运动能力。牙齿和头骨支持水生捕食的解释，但没有直接记录具体猎物。上下摆动游泳、类似水獭的水中运动以及类似海狮的陆上运动，都是与现生动物作出的比较，并非对化石动物运动表现的观察。

title.en: Fossil evidence for the origin of aquatic locomotion in archaeocete whales
title.zh: Fossil evidence for the origin of aquatic locomotion in archaeocete whales

scope.en: Thewissen et al. (1994), pp. 210?212, Figures 1?3: H-GSP 18507 anatomy, Kuldana Formation context and functional comparisons of terrestrial and aquatic movement.

readerLimitations.en: These interpretations rest on the partial holotype from the Kuldana Formation in Pakistan. The cited material does not define a full body-size range, exact swimming style, land performance or a genus-wide feeding pattern.
readerLimitations.zh: 这些解释依据的是巴基斯坦库尔达纳组出土的部分正模标本。所引材料未能确定完整的体型范围、确切游泳方式、陆地运动能力或整个属的取食模式。

traitsZh: 前肢和后肢发达，能够承重。
用于运动比较的椎骨与四肢特征组合。

overview: Aegicetus gehennae is anchored by the associated holotype CGM 60584 from the lower Gehannam Formation at Wadi Al Hitan. Its long posterior trunk, unfused sacral vertebrae, lack of a weight-bearing sacroiliac joint and reduced limbs inform a model of increasingly tail-driven swimming; no tail fluke is securely preserved.
overviewZh: Aegicetus gehennae 以 Wadi Al Hitan（鲸谷）下部 Gehannam 组的关联正模 CGM 60584 为依据。其后躯干较长、骶椎未融合、缺少承重的骶髂关节且四肢缩小；这些结构被用于提出尾部推进作用增强的游泳模型，但没有可靠保存尾鳍。

ecology.diet: Marine predation is inferred from cetacean teeth; prey is not preserved.
ecology.habitat: The known material comes from a marine lower Gehannam depositional setting at Wadi Al Hitan.
ecology.locomotion: Mid-body and tail undulation is inferred; a tail fluke is not preserved.
ecology.bodySize: A large protocetid represented by substantial associated remains; no exact body length is assigned here.
ecology.guild: Marine predation is inferred from anatomy rather than observed feeding.
ecology.dietZh: 根据鲸类牙齿推断其在海洋中捕食；未保存猎物。
ecology.habitatZh: 已知材料来自 Wadi Al Hitan 的海相下 Gehannam 沉积环境。
ecology.locomotionZh: 研究推断其中段身体和尾部会摆动；化石未保存尾鳍。
ecology.bodySizeZh: 一种由较完整关联遗骸代表的大型原鲸科成员；此处未给出确切体长。
ecology.guildZh: 海洋捕食是根据解剖特征推断，并非观察到摄食行为。

traits: Unfused sacrals without a weight-bearing sacroiliac joint
Reduced limbs; a tail fluke is not securely preserved
evidenceSummary: CGM 60584 documents the locomotor anatomy used in the study’s model. The displayed 37.71 Ma point sits amid competing stratigraphic interpretations; it is not an exact specimen date, a first or last appearance, or observed swimming performance.

readerLimitations.en: The 37.71 Ma point is a display value amid competing stratigraphic interpretations, not an exact date for CGM 60584 or a genus endpoint. Predation and tail-driven swimming are anatomical hypotheses; prey, performance and a tail fluke are not directly documented.
readerLimitations.zh: 37.71 Ma 是在存在地层解释分歧时采用的展示点，不是 CGM 60584 的精确年代，也不是属的首末现时间。捕食与尾部推进游泳属于解剖学假说；猎物、游泳表现和尾鳍都未被直接记录。

evidenceSummaryZh: CGM 60584 记录了研究模型所用的运动解剖特征。图示的 37.71 Ma 时间点处于相互竞争的地层解释之间；它不是该标本的精确年代、最早或最晚出现时间，也不是观察到的游泳表现。
traitsZh: 骶椎未融合，也没有承重的骶髂关节。
肢体退化；尾鳍是否存在尚无可靠保存证据。

commonNameZh: 地点组合的陆生早期鲸
geography: H-GSP Locality 62, Ganda Kas, Kala Chitta Hills, Punjab, Pakistan
overview: The familiar “wolf-sized Pakicetus” reconstruction combines skull H-GSP 96231 with vertebrae and limb bones catalogued separately from H-GSP Locality 62. The skull’s ear region and the weight-bearing limbs support an early whale with substantial terrestrial locomotor ability.

ecology.diet: Diet is unresolved from the described skeleton and teeth; the study does not attribute prey remains to the sample
ecology.habitat: Terrestrial use is inferred from the locomotor skeleton; the locality and formation do not prove a shoreline microhabitat
ecology.locomotion: Running and terrestrial locomotion are inferred from limb proportions and osteology; performance was not observed
ecology.bodySize: Wolf-sized pakicetid in the authors' comparison
ecology.guild: Terrestrial early-cetacean interpretation with ecological guild bounded to the named sample

traits: Cetacean-like basicranial ear region in skull H-GSP 96231
Weight-bearing limbs and running adaptations in separately catalogued postcrania
evidenceSummary: The skull and postcranial bones come from the same locality but are not one associated skeleton. Their anatomy supports a terrestrial body-plan interpretation; it does not establish a specific shoreline habitat, and Pakicetus is not presented here as a direct ancestor.

text.en: The familiar “wolf-sized Pakicetus” reconstruction combines skull H-GSP 96231 with vertebrae and limb bones catalogued separately from H-GSP Locality 62. The skull’s ear region and the weight-bearing limbs support an early whale with substantial terrestrial locomotor ability.
text.zh: 常见的狼大小 Pakicetus 复原把头骨 H-GSP 96231 与分别编目的椎骨和肢骨组合在一起；这些颅后材料来自 H-GSP 62 号地点。头骨耳区和承重肢骨支持早期鲸类具有显著陆地运动能力的解释。

title.en: A skull and separate postcranial bones
title.zh: 头骨与分别编目的颅后骨骼

text.en:
The basicranial region of skull H-GSP 96231 has cetacean-like ear features. Separately catalogued postcranial material preserves weight-bearing limb bones and features associated with running.

The reconstruction combines several unassociated specimens from the same locality.
text.zh:
头骨 H-GSP 96231 的基底颅区具有鲸类样耳部特征。

分别编目的颅后材料保存了承重肢骨及奔跑适应特征。

身体复原组合了同一地点的多件、彼此未关联的标本。

title.en: A terrestrial interpretation from a locality composite
title.zh: 地点组合材料支持的陆地运动解释

text.en: Limb proportions and osteology support a terrestrial locomotor interpretation, not an observed gait. The locality and formation do not establish a shoreline microhabitat, and the cited study does not assign prey remains to the sample. “Wolf-sized” is an author comparison for a locality composite, not a mass measurement; the terrestrial early-cetacean interpretation is bounded to the named sample.
text.zh: 肢骨比例和骨骼结构支持陆地运动的解释，却不是步态的直接观察。地点和地层不能确定岸边微栖地，所引研究也没有把猎物遗骸归入这些样本。“狼大小”是作者对地点组合材料的比较描述，并非体重测量；陆地型早期鲸类解释也仅限于具名样本。

text.en: The skull and postcranial bones come from the same locality but are not one associated skeleton. Their anatomy supports a terrestrial body-plan interpretation; it does not establish a specific shoreline habitat, and Pakicetus is not presented here as a direct ancestor.
text.zh: 头骨和颅后骨骼来自同一地点，却不是同一具相互关联的骨架。它们的解剖结构支持陆地型身体构型的解释，但不能确定具体岸边栖地；本页也不把 Pakicetus 写成直接祖先。

title.en: Skeletons of terrestrial cetaceans and the relationship of whales to artiodactyls
title.zh: Skeletons of terrestrial cetaceans and the relationship of whales to artiodactyls

scope.en: The Pakicetus reconstruction combines a skull and separately catalogued postcranial bones from one locality, not one associated skeleton.
scope.zh: Pakicetus 复原组合了同一地点的头骨与分别编目的颅后骨骼，并非一具关联骨架。

geography: Lowest Yumaque Member, Paracas Formation, Playa Media Luna, Pisco Basin, Peru
overview: Holotype MUSM 3580 is a partial skeleton from the middle Eocene Yumaque Member of coastal Peru; its sacral attachment, robust limbs and hoof-like phalanges document a quadrupedal whale with both aquatic and weight-bearing anatomical signals.

ecology.diet: Carnivory is inferred from cetacean dentition; prey and feeding behaviour are not preserved
ecology.habitat: Marine depositional context is documented, while amphibious habitat use is inferred from the skeleton
ecology.locomotion: Quadrupedal swimming and terrestrial weight bearing are functional reconstructions; no gait or swimming performance was observed
ecology.bodySize: Approximately 4 m long according to the reported skeletal dimensions
ecology.guild: Amphibious quadrupedal cetacean interpretation with route and behaviour unresolved

traits: Partial articulated holotype MUSM 3580 preserving mandibles and most major postcranial regions
Two fused sacrals, defined femoral head and hoof-like distal phalanges
Functional hind limbs alongside aquatic cetacean adaptations
evidenceSummary: MUSM 3580 fixes an approximately 42.6 Ma Peruvian protocetid occurrence and preserves anatomy consistent with weight bearing and aquatic locomotion; walking, swimming and westward dispersal remain analytical interpretations, not direct ancestry.

title.en: Hind feet still matter in this whale
title.zh: 这具鲸类骨架仍保留了重要的后足

text.en:
Holotype MUSM 3580 is a partial, articulated skeleton from Peru’s middle Eocene Yumaque Member, dated in the dossier to about 42.6 million years ago. It preserves the jaws, much of the axial skeleton and portions of the limbs. Two fused sacral vertebrae, a defined femoral head and hoof-like toe bones show how much of the hind-limb apparatus remains available for comparison.

Those structures occur together with cetacean aquatic adaptations, so Peregocetus records a body plan that had not lost all weight-bearing limb anatomy. The fossils support a mixed functional reconstruction, not a witnessed walk or swim, and its placement among protocetids does not establish direct ancestry of later whales.
text.zh:
正模 MUSM 3580 是来自秘鲁中始新世 Yumaque 段的一具部分关节相连骨架，档案所引年代约为 4,260 万年前。标本保存了下颌、相当部分的中轴骨骼及部分肢体。两块愈合的骶椎、明确的股骨头和蹄状趾骨，显示后肢结构有多少仍可供比较。

这些结构与鲸类的水生适应同时出现，因此 Peregocetus 记录了一种尚未丢失所有承重肢体解剖的体制。化石支持的是混合功能的复原，而非直接观察到行走或游泳；它在原鲸科中的位置也不能证明它是后期鲸类的直系祖先。

title.en: An amphibious whale from the middle Eocene of Peru reveals early South Pacific dispersal of quadrupedal cetaceans
title.zh: An amphibious whale from the middle Eocene of Peru reveals early South Pacific dispersal of quadrupedal cetaceans
